Thank you, Aguinaldo. Before I open the floor, the first question is mine. Is that your opinion, or is it what the research shows?
Both, and I try to keep them apart. It is widely believed that early termination is rare in Brazil. My data suggest it is not.
That is a strong claim. What is your evidence?
Forty-two contracts over twenty years. Early termination has been found to happen in about one in five of them. That supports my hypothesis.
Is that a correlation, or can you show the cause?
For now, only a correlation. Most terminations are thought to start with a tariff dispute, but I cannot prove that yet. That is the main limitation of the study.
I appreciate the honesty. Is there a consensus in the literature, or is the question still open?
Still open. The results so far are inconclusive. That is why I would like an authority on concession law to weigh in.

Good afternoon, and welcome to the doctoral seminar. A few words before our first speaker. Each presentation is ten minutes, followed by ten minutes of questions. In ten minutes you cannot say everything, so please choose one question and one finding. When you present the work of other scholars, be fair. Say what is generally believed, and say what has been shown, but keep that separate from your own view. We want to hear clearly where the literature ends and where you begin. And please be honest about your limitations. In this room, a limitation is not a weakness. A study that hides its limits is. Our first speaker is a lawyer and a former CEO, and his topic is the early termination of infrastructure concessions.

I have been asked to give my opinion on one question: does early termination cost the state more than a normal contract? Let me start with what we know. It is widely believed that the state saves money when it takes a concession back. That belief is understandable, but the evidence does not support it. In the cases I studied, the cost of a new tender, the legal claims and the months without investment were found to be higher than the savings in almost every case. Now, what we do not know. The data on smaller contracts are inconclusive, and I would not draw conclusions from them. So my opinion, as an expert, is this: early termination should be a last resort, not a first reaction. And I am happy to take questions.
